label: Person
name: Adolfo Zon Pereira
summary:
Adolfo Zon Pereira is a Brazilian Roman Catholic bishop, part of the vast Brazilian episcopate that serves the world's largest national Catholic population. His ministry in Brazil reflects the complexities of a Church that has been central to Brazilian national identity since the Portuguese colonial period but now navigates a dramatically changed religious landscape.

Brazil's religious transformation in the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries has been one of the most dramatic in Catholic history. In 1970 Brazil was 92% Catholic; today that figure has fallen below 50% in many surveys, with Pentecostalism now claiming the allegiance of approximately 30% of the population. This shift has profoundly challenged the Catholic Church's assumptions about its social role and institutional security.

Zon Pereira's episcopal service takes place in this context of radical religious change, requiring pastoral leadership that can respond to a more competitive religious marketplace, maintain the Church's extensive social service networks, and renew its evangelistic witness for a generation that has been exposed to compelling Pentecostal alternatives. His ministry reflects the Brazilian Church's urgent work of renewal and self-examination.
